name: Nixsora and vexxloso public company/account cluster

attribution.legal_posture: Publisher research assessment; legal charge, conviction, and verified legal-identity status remain unestablished.

caveats: Preserve this negative finding to avoid equating suspicious persona or recruiting activity with malware.
Publish as a research-attributed suspected front-company relationship; legal status remains research attribution.

Relationships are the publisher's public OSINT assessment based on account follows, reused profile imagery, website content, repository review and cross-platform posting; legal identity and nationality remain unestablished for each persona.
Account-to-cluster relationships are retained only. Copied imagery is contextual material; pictured-person involvement or identity requires source support.
The record covers only public account relationships and recruiting behavior; legal identity remains unverified.
Treat James Jhon as a research-attributed persona; legal identity remains unverified.

statements: North Korean Internet assesses Nixsora as a newly created company/front-company presentation that appeared after much of the earlier Mentonex-linked cluster went offline. Its public job pages sought blockchain developers, while its community pages contained conversations pre-seeded in the site's public code.

The public GitHub account vexxloso was linked by the source to the earlier Mentonex persona cluster through followers trader389 and walletdiscover1010-a11y; trader389 reused the image of a Mentonex Slack persona, while walletdiscover1010-a11y remained associated with Mentonex.

A public persona presented as James Jhon used the same profile image as vexxloso and posted repeatedly on Dev.to about a sports-card project, while removed search-index results indicated additional community posting. The source interprets this as credibility building around the Nixsora recruitment cluster.

The source linked recruiter-test to Nixsora through follower/account pivots and noted blockchain-themed test repositories; lightart732059 was part of the same public cluster and advertised remote profit-sharing work.
The publisher explicitly reported finding no malicious code in the reviewed repositories, despite assessing the cluster as part of a broader recruitment campaign.
